Fix only the physically awkward pose: this currently looks like her shoulder is in the water and her chin rests directly on it. Pull the camera back to a medium-wide 3:2 view. Her chin is well clear of the water; a visible band of AIR and distant stone bank separates her real profile from the water surface, and an equally clear separation from its inverted reflection. She is not swimming, lying on water or touching water with her face. View across a broad, still pool from a low side viewpoint. Keep the same female marble statue, the same shoulder brooch and coiled bun, and maintain a clear optical reflection DIRECTLY below her, vertically inverted, nose still pointing to the right, same bun, eye, brow, and brooch. Water reflection slightly darker; very gentle ripples only at the outer corners. Frame both real and reflected faces comfortably inside the central square of the landscape photo. Keep lived-in courtyard, old matte stone and directional natural light. Foreground water and stone lip make it unmistakably a real pool, not a Photoshop mirror. No new figures, no glow or decorative effects.
current.initialPrompt: Correct this editorial photograph of a Greek marble woman looking at herself in a pool. The current reflected face slides far right and has different features and angle. Recompose the shot as necessary to make the reflection GEOMETRICALLY UNMISTAKABLE and the central subject: use a near water-level camera with its axis horizontal, fixed side-on profile of a single weathered marble woman leaning over still horizontal water, face above water facing RIGHT. Compose the eye, nose tip and curls clearly on the same vertical plumb lines in the upper face and the upside-down lower reflection. Reflection is an optically inverted view of the SAME head and shoulders (same nose pointing RIGHT, same carved hair knot, same brow, same drapery), suspended straight beneath the subject across the horizontal waterline, NOT rotated 180 degrees, not looking back left, not displaced elsewhere in the pool. Put her face above the water itself, NOT above a solid ledge; view across the pond toward the woman on its far bank. Use a low enough viewpoint that very little of the underside of her chin is seen. A hint of darker water and a minute ripple outside the face can distinguish the reflected half; keep the reflected face clearly recognizable, not distorted. Keep hair bun, drapery, weathered marble, quiet courtyard daylight and meditative mood. Build the entire composition around that one identifiable profile and its clear inverted twin. No extra people, no second actual statue, no lettering. Horizontal 3:2 composition with both faces fully inside the central square crop, full face and reflection in frame.

current.concept: One seated statue offers a shallow carved bowl to another at a spring. Their hands and the bowl carry the act of kindness.
current.prompt: A quiet editorial photograph of a single ancient Greek marble sculptural group: two life-size human figures seated together on the edge of a worn stone spring, one offering water to the other. The older figure on the left extends ONE simple shallow Greek drinking bowl, held at its solid base. The younger adult on the right leans slightly forward and opens one palm just below the rim to accept it. The little slice of space between the hands shows the moment of kindness; no forced expressions or power pose. Both sit at equal eye level. Bowl, two bodies and all visible drapery are carved from the same mottled, grey, weathered limestone, like a surviving group sculpture that a photographer encountered in a quiet ancient courtyard. Real carved eyes, grazed edges, individual chisel cuts; age is uneven around the sheltered folds. Close enough to read the simple human gesture at phone size. One natural shaft of open-sky light comes from the side. Restrained ash and chalk palette. One coherent period and material, without lamps, food, packaging, modern people, signs, costumes from a film, text or graphic effects. No other objects in the hands. 3:2 landscape, eye-level three-quarter view, the bowl easy to identify, both faces and the offered bowl grouped in the center.

current.prompt: A quiet archaeological editorial photograph of an entirely ancient Greek domestic interior just after someone has left a game unfinished. The focal point is the absence: one empty, slightly crooked wooden low stool pulled back from a plain limestone table, seen through a shadowed doorway. On that table only: a pair of worn bone dice resting among a few coins, a small stoppered terracotta remedy flask, and a closed wax writing tablet with its stylus set aside. The objects suggest gambling, relief and a lesson left unread; they occupy a single little pool of side light and must not look arranged for museum display. Spare worn limeplaster walls with exposed stone at the threshold, a repaired plank door, scuffed floor, cool early daylight from the courtyard, a little warmth in clay. Modest lived-in ancient house, no monumental pillars or temple, nobody in the room. No electricity, TV, laptop, contemporary furniture, glass bottles, cables, screens, written text or logos. Gritty, grounded, tactile, quiet ash tones and natural light, not luxurious, no glowing fantasy elements. Medium-wide horizontal 16:9 composition from doorway, with empty seat large enough to read on a blog card.
